This is the corrected occlusion logic surfaced in the deliverable UI, not just the probe.

Port block is a hotspot (click zooms to the jacks) and reads as reachable from the front. SFP: final authorized lever applied (port_shield envMap 1.30->1.70), declared honestly as a render dial past physical (no AO in scene, so the sleeve already receives full environment) — the last turn, no more rounds, consistent with the shared conclusion that the RJ45/SFP distinction is genuinely subtle at real scale.
Diagnostic column is a hotspot (click toggles the LED plate on/off); reachable from front. Labels read. No regression.
Top terminals are a hotspot (click shows the DIN rail); reachable from front. No regression.

defects: None blocking. The SFP pop remains subtle even after the final envMap lever; accepted as the honest real-scale limit (no further rounds).
corrections: SCENE/LIBRARY: the corrected pick() (stop at first visible surface; blockedBy names the occluder) must be the standard when this and the other assets are integrated, because cross-equipment occlusion is the case that makes the bug manifest.

Hotspots: port block -> zoom jacks, diagnostic column -> toggle LED plate, top terminals -> show DIN rail, rear latch -> rotate to rear view.

notes: Inline orchestrator judgment. The interaction deliverable is present and correct, and it earned its pass on a real find: the occlusion test was pass-through (pick() skipped non-hotspot hits and continued through solid geometry, so the rear latch reported clickable from the FRONT where the housing fully hides it). It stayed invisible on the PDU only because every PDU occluder happens to be a hotspot. Fixed: pick() stops at the first visible surface (a real click cannot pass through a solid body) and blockedBy now NAMES the occluder so a probe can tell an occluded hotspot from a non-existent one. The fix is visible in the deliverable itself (Pestillo DIN correctly dimmed from the front). Cleared to the optimization pass. See PDU DEFERRED-CORRECTIONS for the same-latent-bug decision.
